text:
Given below are two statements: 

Statement I : An electric dipole is placed at the center of a hollow sphere. The flux of the electric field through the sphere is zero but the electric field is not zero anywhere in the sphere.

Statement II : If R is the radius of a solid metallic sphere and Q be the total charge on it. The electric field at any point on the spherical surface of radius r (< R) is zero but the electric flux passing through this closed spherical surface of radius r is not zero.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Net charge on electric dipole = + q $-$ q = 0

Hence, according to Gauss's law,

Electric flux, $𝜙=\frac{q_{net}}{ε_{0}}=\frac{0}{ε_{0}}=0$

Electric field due to electric dipole is non-zero and varies at point to point.

Hence, statement I is true.

Electric field due to charged solid sphere at a distance r from centre.

$E=\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}.\frac{Qr}{R^{3}}$ [when r < R, R $\to$ radius] which is non-zero.

Hence, statement II is false.

Hence, option (c) is the correct.

text: A wire of 1$\Omega$ has a length of 1 m. It is stretched till its length increases by 25%. The percentage change in resistance to the nearest integer is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$R_{0} = 1\Omega$

$R_{1} =$ ?

$l_{0} = 1m$

$l_{1} = 1.25 m$

$A_{0} = A$

As volume of wire remains constant so

$A_{0}l_{0} = A_{1}l_{1}$ $\Rightarrow$ $A_{1} =$ $\frac{l_{0}A_{0}}{l_{1}}$

Now

Resistance (R) = $\frac{pl}{A}$

$\frac{R_{0}}{R_{1}}=\frac{l_{0}}{A_{0}}\left (\frac{l_{0}A_{0}}{l_{1}\times l_{1}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $R_{1}=\frac{l_{1}^{2}}{l_{0}^{2}}=1.5625\Omega$

So % change in resistance 

$=\frac{R_{1}-R_{0}}{R_{0}}\times 100%$

$=\frac{1.5625-1}{1}\times 100%$

$=56.25%$

text: The length of metallic wire is $l_{1}$ when tension in it is $T_{1}$. It is $l_{2}$ when the tension is $T_{2}$. The original length of the wire will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Assuming Hooke's law to be valid.

$T\propto (\Delta l)$

$T=k(\Delta l)$

Let, $l_{0} =$ natural length (original length)

$\Rightarrow T=k(l-l_{0})$

so, $T_{1}=k(l_{1}-l_{0})$ & $T_{2}=k(l_{2}-l_{0})$

$\Rightarrow \frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\frac{l_{1}-l_{0}}{l_{2}-l_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow l_{0}=\frac{T_{2}l_{1}-T_{1}l_{2}}{T_{2}-T_{1}}$

text: The trajectory of a projectile in a vertical plane is y = $α$x $-$ $βx^{2}$, where $α$ and $β$ are constants and x & y are respectively the horizontal and vertical distances of the projectile from the point of projection. solution.body:
y = $α$x $-$ $βx^{2}$

comparing with trajectory equation

$y=x\tan θ-\frac{1}{2}\frac{gx^{2}}{u^{2}\cos ^{2}θ}$

$\tan θ=α\Rightarrow θ=\tan ^{-1}α$

$β=\frac{1}{2}\frac{g}{u^{2}\cos ^{2}θ}$

$\Rightarrow$ $u^{2}=\frac{g}{2β\cos ^{2}θ}$

Maximum height H :

$H=\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}θ}{2g}=\frac{g}{2β\cos ^{2}θ}\frac{\sin ^{2}θ}{2g}$

$\Rightarrow$ $H=\frac{\tan ^{2}θ}{4β}=\frac{α^{2}}{4β}$

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labeled as Assertion A and the other is labeled as Reason R.

Assertion A : For a simple microscope, the angular size of the object equals the angular size of the image.

Reason R : Magnification is achieved as the small object can be kept much closer to the eye than 25 cm and hence it subtends a large angle.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With the eye close to the lens, the object and its virtual image lie on the same rays through the optical centre, so both subtend the same angle at the eye; Assertion A is true.

Without the lens the object must be kept at about $25\text{cm}$ to be seen distinctly; the lens allows it to be kept much closer, where it subtends a larger angle, while its image is formed at a comfortable distance. This is how angular magnification arises, so Reason R is true.

R accounts for the magnification obtained despite the equality stated in A; it does not explain why the angular sizes of object and image are equal, which follows from the ray geometry alone.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift

text: A particle executes S.H.M., the graph of velocity as a function of displacement is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a body performing SHM, relation between velocity and displacement

$v=ω\sqrt{A^{2}-x^{2}}$

now, square both side

$v^{2}=w^{2}(A^{2}-x^{2})$

$\Rightarrow v^{2}=w^{2}A^{2}-ω^{2}x^{2}$

$v^{2}+ω^{2}x^{2}=ω^{2}A^{2}$

divide whole equation by $ω^{2}A^{2}$

$\frac{v^{2}}{ω^{2}A^{2}}+\frac{ω^{2}x^{2}}{ω^{2}A^{2}}=\frac{ω^{2}x^{2}}{ω^{2}A^{2}}$

$\frac{v^{2}}{(ωA)^{2}}+\frac{x^{2}}{(A)^{2}}=1$

above equation is similar as standard equation of ellipses, so graph between velocity and displacement will be ellipses.

text: Time period of a simple pendulum is T. The time taken to complete $\frac{5}{8}$ oscillations starting from mean position is $\frac{α}{β}T$. The value of $α$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
One complete oscillation covers a path of $4A$, so $\dfrac{5}{8}$ oscillation is a path of $\dfrac{5}{8}\times 4A=\dfrac{5A}{2}$.

Starting from the mean position, the first $2A$ (mean to extreme and back to mean) takes $\dfrac{T}{2}$.

The remaining $\dfrac{A}{2}$ starts again from the mean position: $x=A\sin ωt^{'}=\dfrac{A}{2}$ gives $ωt^{'}=\dfrac{π}{6}$, so $t^{'}=\dfrac{π/6}{2π/T}=\dfrac{T}{12}$.

Total time:

$t=\dfrac{T}{2}+\dfrac{T}{12}=\dfrac{7T}{12}$

So $α=7$ and $β=12$.

Hence, the answer is 7.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift

text: The volume V of a given mass of monoatomic gas changes with temperature T according to the relation $V=KT^{\frac{2}{3}}$. The workdone when temperature changes by 90K will be xR. The value of x is $_________$. [R = universal gas constant]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that work done is 

$W=\int PdV$ .... (1)

$\Rightarrow P=\frac{nRT}{V}$ .... (2)

$\Rightarrow W=\int \frac{nRT}{V}dv$ .... (3)

and given $V=KT^{2/3}$ .... (4)

$\Rightarrow W=\int \frac{nRT}{KT^{2/3}}.dv$ .... (5)

$\Rightarrow$ from (4) : $dv=\frac{2}{3}KT^{-1/3}dT$

$\Rightarrow W=\int\limits _{T_{1}}^{T_{2}}\frac{nRT}{KT^{2/3}}\frac{2}{3}K\frac{1}{T^{1/3}}dT$

$\Rightarrow W=\frac{2}{3}nR\times (T_{2}-T_{1})$ .... (6)

$\Rightarrow T_{2}-T_{1}=90K$ .... (7)

$\Rightarrow W=\frac{2}{3}nR\times 90$

$\Rightarrow W=60nR$

Assuming 1 mole of gas

n = 1

So, W = 60R

In the reported figure of earth, the value of acceleration due to gravity is same at point A and C but it is smaller than that of its value at point B (surface of the earth). The value of OA : AB will be x : y. The value of x is $________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$g_{A}=\frac{GM(r)}{R^{3}}$

$g_{C}=\frac{GM}{\left (R+\frac{R}{2}\right )^{2}}$

Given, $g_{A} = g_{C}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{GM(r)}{R^{3}}=\frac{GM}{\left (R+\frac{R}{2}\right )^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{r}{R^{3}}=\frac{4}{9R^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow r=\frac{4R}{9}$

$\therefore$ $OA=\frac{4R}{9}$

$\therefore$ $AB=R-r=\frac{5R}{9}$

$\therefore$ $OA:AB=4:5$

$\therefore$ x = 4

text: Two streams of photons, possessing energies equal to twice and ten times the work function of metal are incident on the metal surface successively. The value of ratio of maximum velocities of the photoelectrons emitted in the two respective cases is x : y. The value of x is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$KE_{\max }=hv-𝜙$

$\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}=hv-𝜙$

$v=\sqrt{\frac{2(hv-𝜙)}{m}}$

Given $hv_{1}=2𝜙$

$hv_{2}=10𝜙$

$\therefore$ $\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{hv_{1}-𝜙}{hv_{2}-𝜙}}$

$\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{2𝜙-𝜙}{10𝜙-𝜙}}=\frac{1}{3}$ = $\frac{x}{y}$

$\therefore$ x = 1
